sources.title: Saudipedia, Unification of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Official historical encyclopedia. Direct full page checked for 1902 Riyadh, 1913 al-Ahsa, 1921 Ha’il and 23 September 1932. Use these dated facts, not celebratory explanations or internally inconsistent Hijaz campaign chronology.

sources.title: Memorandum on British Commitments to Bin Saud, 1918
sources.note: British Library IOR/L/PS/18/B295, printed p. 15, folio 129r. English treaty text of 26 December 1915, articles I to V. Indexed original transcription checked. Treaty requirements are intentions and obligations, not proof of compliance.

sources.title: H. St J. B. Philby, Southern Nejd: Journey to Kharj, Aflaj, Sulaiyyil, and Wadi Dawasir in 1918
sources.note: British Library IOR/L/PS/20/C169, Cairo 1919. Indexed original pages 40 (folio 24v) and 49 (folio 29r) checked, plus catalogue itinerary. Group every page, downloadable PDF and later reuse in The Heart of Arabia conservatively. Colonial observer’s specific observations are attributed; cultural rankings are not adopted.

sources.title: Robert Edward Hamilton, Diary of a journey to Najd, submitted February 1918
sources.note: IOR/R/15/5/104, printed p. 10, folio 20v, direct full transcription. Cover at folio 16r dates submission 1 February 1918 and diary begins 9 October, indicating the preceding 1917 journey despite catalogue title Visit to Nejd 1918. Public prose says wartime diary and assigns no synthetic year.

sources.title: Guido Steinberg, Ecology, Knowledge, and Trade in Central Arabia
sources.note: EUI working-paper version, printed p. 18. Indexed original full page checked via query site:cadmus.eui.eu Najd inheritance; direct PDF fetch failed. Scope is nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Related 2004 chapter DOI 10.1057/9781403981318_4 grouped as the same work.

sources.title: Karine Walther, What Went Wrong? U.S. Diplomatic History in the Era of COVID-19
sources.note: Diplomatic History 45(3), 2021, pp. 631 to 642. Direct full article accessed through publisher redirect. Opening Harrison case and cited 18 January 1919 letter checked. Avoid contested death counts, royal-family counts and claims that care cured influenza.

sources.title: Guido Steinberg, Seuchen und Krieg im Jahr der Gnade
sources.note: Freie Universität Berlin, 2002, direct full German essay. Local al-Bassam chronicle extracts on livestock care used. Do not adopt obsolete virology, mortality totals or speculative origin theories. Group with Steinberg Najd study conservatively.

sources.title: Qatar Digital Library, St John Philby’s Mission to Najd: Across the Heart of Arabia
sources.note: British Library curatorial article, indexed full original checked. Practical and Diplomatic Logistics: al-Nafisi’s messenger assistance, Kodak film, watches and tents. Watch recipients are explicitly conjectural in the source.

sources.title: Saeed Mushabab Al-Qahtani, The Visit of Najd Delegation to London, October to November 1919
sources.note: Dirasat Human and Social Sciences 50(5), Supplement 1 (2023), pp. 566 to 580, DOI 10.35516/hum.v50i5.367. Full article English text read at ResearchGate publication 376838785. Letter translation printed p. 570; Arabic facsimile Appendix I p. 576. Original-script words could not be verified visually by author or root, so the public passage deliberately uses only the checked translation.

proposedOverrides.summary: Wartime Najdi towns, rival rulers, oasis farming, diplomacy and household life before the Saudi kingdom.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact 1914 to 1920 regional record only; no aliases or dynastic continuity override.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two world-1914 geometries, one broad Arabian interior polygon and a detached Musandam-area sliver. Main polygon includes Riyadh, Ha’il, Hofuf and Buraydah, excludes Mecca, Medina, Muscat, Kuwait and Doha. Public overview explicitly rejects an Ibn Saud border reading.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Keep nejd (1783 to 1878), arabia (1878 to 1914), ancient pastoral-nomad record, Saudi Arabia and Ottoman Empire cards distinct. Ha’il was conquered after this interval, in 1921.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No house-level sanitation evidence securely dated to this interval was established. Do not fill that gap with present-day heritage reconstructions. Contemporary European accounts are attributed, with ethnic and cultural rankings rejected.
